results.question: How much is the monthly fee on the everyday account and how do I avoid paying it?
results.answer:
The Kaskazi Everyday Account costs **KES 250 a month**. You do not pay it in any month when your salary is paid into the account, or when your average balance for the month is KES 50,000 or more.

There are two ways to avoid it:
- **Salary:** The KES 250 monthly fee is waived for any month in which your salary is paid into your Kaskazi Everyday Account. Money you move yourself from another account, cash paid in, money from a mobile money wallet, and payments from friends or family do not count as salary.
- **Average balance:** Kaskazi Bank adds up the balance in your Kaskazi Everyday Account at the end of each day of the month, then divides by the number of days in the month. The balance can fall below KES 50,000 on some days and you can still qualify, as long as the average for the whole month is KES 50,000 or more.

If you are self-employed or paid in cash, you won't qualify for the salary waiver, but you can still use the average balance waiver.

results.question: why cant i withdraw more than 20k a day from my student acount??
results.answer:
The KES 20,000 daily limit is there to protect students' money. Students often carry cash on campus and share accommodation. If your card and PIN are stolen, the most a thief can take in cash in a day is KES 20,000.

The limit covers all cash withdrawals added together: at Kaskazi Bank ATMs, at other banks' ATMs, at Kaskazi agents and at branches. It can't be raised on a Kaskazi Student Account.

For large payments such as rent or fees, pay by transfer or card instead of cash. School fees payments from your Kaskazi account are free. Card payments in shops and online are not cash withdrawals, so they don't count towards the KES 20,000.

When the account converts to a Kaskazi Everyday Account, the standard Kaskazi Debit Card ATM limit of KES 100,000 a day applies from then on.
